bugs: Public filters are validated by a FormRequest, so a bad value (for example ?sort=bogus or a stale category slug) sends a 302 back to the previous URL, or to '/' when there is none, instead of ignoring the bad filter. Impl-2 does the same.

If both name and slug are empty, prepareForValidation produces an empty slug, so a 'slug required' error appears next to the 'name required' error, which is noisy (app/Http/Requests/Admin/ProductRequest.php:13).
antipatterns: app/Models/Product.php:77-78 uses whereRaw with escape '!' to search with LIKE. The wildcard escaping is correct, but the raw SQL is heavier than it needs to be.
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:20 builds the sort options with collect($sorts)->mapWithKeys(...) inside the view. The controller could pass these ready-made.
tests/Feature/Admin/ProductManagementTest.php:7 declares a global validProduct() function in a test file, which can collide with other test files.
tests/Feature/Admin/ProductManagementTest.php:27 uses a hard-to-read ternary to decide which routes need the product parameter.
strengths: The single product form is a real <x-product-form> component, used for both create and edit. The form/input, select, textarea, checkbox and error components use @props, $attributes->class()->merge() and @error, and mark invalid fields with an is-invalid class.
The checkbox sends a hidden 0 value, so an unchecked box stays unchecked after a failed submit (confirmed by a probe).
@session in the flash component; the Paginator::defaultView custom pagination works without compiled assets; the query string is kept with withQueryString().
Uses #[Scope] attributes, Attribute::get for formatted_price, whereBelongsTo, whereRelation, Rule::enum with an enum label(), Model::shouldBeStrict, and to_route.
Escapes % and _ in search terms so they match literally (confirmed by a probe), and shows filter validation errors on the catalogue page.
The slug is generated from the name when left empty, and the categories foreign key cascades on delete.
Thorough Pest tests: datasets, an authorization matrix, validation messages, old input, pagination links, related products, and LIKE wildcards.

bugs: Old input is lost for the 'Active' checkbox. There is no hidden 0 input, and the value merged in prepareForValidation is not part of the flashed old input. So if an admin unchecks Active and validation fails, the edit form shows the box checked again. A probe confirmed this (resources/views/components/form/checkbox.blade.php:4).
Search does not escape LIKE wildcards, so ?q=% matches every product (confirmed by a probe) (app/Models/Product.php:66).
When a filter is invalid, the request redirects back with errors, but the catalogue filter form has no @error output, so the user sees no message (resources/views/products/index.blade.php:4-18).
The category foreign key has no on-delete rule, so deleting a category that has products throws a QueryException (database/migrations/2026_11_07_000002_create_products_table.php:13).
antipatterns: resources/views/products/index.blade.php:5,9,14 reads request('q'), request('category') and request('sort') directly in the view instead of using validated filters passed in by the controller.
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:20-27 opens and closes the grid <div> using $loop->first and $loop->last inside @forelse, which is awkward markup.
The shared admin form is an @include partial (admin/products/_form.blade.php) that relies on variables leaking in from the parent view, rather than a component with @props.

The form/input, select, textarea and checkbox components repeat the @error markup instead of using a shared error component, and invalid fields get no styling. Attributes are printed with {{ $attributes }} rather than merge().
Product::formattedPrice() is a plain method instead of an Attribute accessor (minor). The route file keeps the closure for '/'.
tests/Feature/AdminProductTest.php:7 declares a global validProduct() function in a test file.
strengths: Thin controllers, and both the index and admin requests are FormRequests that use Rule::enum and Rule::unique()->ignore(), with attributes() giving clearer error messages.
Uses #[Scope] attributes, whereBelongsTo, and a related() builder that the controller eager-loads with('category').
Validates the slug format with a regex, and adds composite indexes that match the sort queries.
Good Pest tests with datasets for validation and the authorization matrix, plus tests for empty filters and the admin link being visible only to admins.

v.rationale: The two have almost the same structure: matching controllers, FormRequests, #[Scope] scopes, an enum for sorting, and a custom pagination view. Both test suites pass (impl-1: 45 tests, impl-2: 48). Impl-1 ranks first because it meets the Blade requirements more fully. Its shared form is a real component, its form fields use $attributes merge/class with a reusable error component, it uses @session, and it shows validation errors on the public filter form. In probes it handled two edge cases that impl-2 got wrong. Impl-1 keeps an unchecked Active box unchecked after a failed submit; impl-2 shows it checked again, so its old input is wrong for the checkbox. Impl-1 also treats % in a search as a literal character; in impl-2, ?q=% matches every product. Impl-2 also has a missing on-delete rule for categories, silent redirects when filters are invalid, request() calls inside the view, and an @include partial instead of a component.
